tasks.reason: Reproduced the reported rejection on current first-party evidence (source_hash 75f69f52..., observed 2026-11-19T18:23:13.508Z). Assembly of the Bedrock partition produced two offers whose identical (state, validity) group was split into variants that the validation contract calls compactable, so validation rejected the provider with 'offer on-demand state grouping key: contains compactable variants'. Root cause was in canonicalizeApplicability: it applied the 1,024-clause applicability bound to the concatenated clauses of a union before canonical deduplication, so a group with 1,216 evidence-bearing observations establishing only 444 distinct clauses threw 'Applicability clause limit exceeded'. compactApplicabilityChunk caught that selector-limit error and bisected the group by item count, emitting siblings whose combined applicability fits every bound. Repair: canonicalizeApplicability now deduplicates and orders clauses first and enforces the same documented bound on the distinct canonical clauses, which is the shape pricing-schema.ts already caps. Assembly and validation limits, byte budgets and the maximal-compaction contract are unchanged. After the repair the same evidence assembles 154 books/offers with exactly one state per offer, zero compactable state pairs, and proceeds past every grouping check. Residual, explicitly not repaired here: the same partition measures 134,313,730 bytes against the 128 MiB providerPricingBytes budget (96,002 bytes, 0.07% over), so validation now reports 'provider pricing byte limit exceeded' and Bedrock stays on its last verified snapshot. Composition is genuine retained data (observations 65.5 MB, applicability 28.8 MB, no duplicated container metadata), and the limit is an operator-reviewed calibration constant guarded by paired-budget invariants, so resolving it needs an operator budget decision rather than a code repair inside this admission. With 1 MiB of headroom the identical partition validates completely, which shows the reported grouping defect is gone and only that budget remains.

The independent probe changed only the CNY notice to cancel that noon start expressly and make 13:00 operative, leaving USD at noon. tasks.reason: Reproduced against the bytes of the latest failed refresh (fetch.comparison matching_refresh, source_hash e43d605e3013df62...). The pre-repair services parser rejected the owned USD pricing page with an unresolved commercial_source_contract_drift sample 'Search/Fetch: Missing USD server-tool exemption instant', published no Web Search / Web Fetch inventory and reported a pricing dependency failure for https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/. The first-party pages did not remove the commercial section: they kept the reviewed Search & Fetch API heading, rows, per-1,000-successful-requests unit and USD 0.75 / CNY 5 amounts, and reworded only the dated exemption sentence (English: server-side search and web fetch tool calls triggered when calling the model are no longer billed and their returned results are billed as model token usage; Chinese equivalent). The parser required the retired exact sentence strings, so fixed-heading discovery of the still-present section failed. The repair replaces both exact strings with a structured binding: a per-currency statement pattern, required clauses for the unbilled model-triggered scope and the token-billing consequence, and a closing clause; the reviewed instant is parsed from the statement date and Beijing time (hour minus 8) and must equal the reviewed freeFrom boundary 2026-11-18T04:00:00.000Z, so a dropped clause, a moved boundary or a reworded scope is rejected instead of silently accepted. The renamed section, rows and unit kept their existing bindings and the retired heading/header/row remain recorded as drift. Residual omission: the source publishes no per-model web-tool meter for the post-cutover tariff, so none is published; the pre-cutover per-model charge is no longer published and is not backfilled.

The original USD and CNY pricing pages and companion guide distinguish billable direct Search and Fetch requests from model-triggered calls: the calls themselves are not billed after the effective time, but returned content is metered as model tokens. The independent probe replayed the full source bundle as a control, then changed only the USD scope clause to explicitly say the calls incur a separate fee. The candidate still accepted the exemption and published fresh offers. The parser checks for phrases independently, so it can mistake 'no longer billed at the old rate' for 'no longer billed.' The probe reached the website pricing projection; this was not just a parser result. It does not establish that the later matching-refresh bundle is byte-identical to the admitted incident, that the incident removed previously published inventory, or that stored data was corrected.
Expected: When the USD page says model-triggered calls incur a separate fee and the unchanged CNY page and guide say the calls are exempt, reject the conflicting fresh pricing rather than publish it as free. The distinct direct API rates are USD 0.75 or CNY 5 per 1,000 successful requests, not per 1,000 returned results.
Observed: The collector accepted the contradictory bundle. Fresh catalog composition and website projection still produced free model-triggered and numeric direct offers for both Web Search and Web Fetch. The direct rates matched the unmodified full-receipt control. A separate exact-source end-to-end and retention probe was not completed.
